headline: 🎉 **225 WILLOW POINT JUST RETURNED THE FIRST FEEDBACK OF ITS LIFE — AND THE PRICE SURVIVED THE DIRECT QUESTION.** Anna C. of A Squared answered at 9:47 this morning, twenty minutes after your email: her buyers “really liked it,” every concern they raised is cosmetic, and when asked point-blank how $185,000 read against what else they have seen, she did not argue the number at all. ⭐ SHE ALSO CORRECTED THE RECORD: she was COVERING for Lindsey H., so Saturday's 9:00 and noon were ONE buyer party, not two brokerages. 🎯 She left you three answerable questions about the house — answer them today and you are talking to a buyer who liked it and never flinched at the price.

hotSignals.signal: 🎉 FIRST-EVER FEEDBACK ON THIS LISTING, AND THE PRICE WENT UNCHALLENGED. Anna C. of A Squared Properties replied at 9:47 AM, twenty minutes after your email: her buyers “really liked it,” the house “showed very well,” and every concern she raised is cosmetic by her own description. ⭐ You asked point-blank how $185,000 read against what else they have seen — and she did not take up the number at all. 🔍 She also disclosed she was COVERING for Lindsey H., so Saturday's two showings were one buyer party.
hotSignals.action: 🎯 ANSWER HER THREE QUESTIONS TODAY — that is the whole move, and two of the three need your sellers first: is the living-room ceiling crack a settled Sheetrock joint, is crown molding going back in or being cut in with paint, and is the patched laundry-room ceiling an intentional access panel for the bathroom above. ⭐ A buyer who liked the house, never argued the price, and named three fixable cosmetic worries is one clear answer away from a second look. ⚠️ Do NOT let a machine answer this one — she is already in a live thread with you and replied to you personally in twenty minutes.

hotSignals.signal: 🎉 IT CONVERTED. The showings on this address stopped mattering Sunday evening when the seller and the buyers agreed — price, concessions and both sides at two and a half — and the closing office opened the contract for signature at 8:06 this morning. This board's oldest live signal is now a deal.
hotSignals.action: ⚠️ THE CONTRACT IS STILL UNSIGNED AS OF THIS RUN. ⭐ A handshake on Sunday and an unsigned document on Monday is the most fragile state a deal ever occupies — the entire job today is getting signatures on it. 🔍 Also worth closing the loop with the buyer's agent, who asked for a status Friday night and was never answered; the answer is now a good one. ⚠️ These buyers must still close their own house first, so this is a contingency, not a closing.

hotSignals.signal: 🎯 A FIFTH SHOWING SATURDAY AT 3:00 PM from an agent who had never shown this house before — the first genuinely new eyes on it in a week, and it came one day after a fourth independent read called the price too high.
hotSignals.action: 🔍 THE READ HAS NOW BEEN OUTSTANDING TWO FULL DAYS. This address does return forms roughly half the time, so it is still an open question rather than a no — but the odds are falling and a direct call to that agent is the faster instrument now. ⭐ THE LEVER THAT IS NOT A PRICE CUT: the last read scored staging one out of five and named unknowns as the objection, and a pre-inspection is exactly what removes unknowns. 🎯 One named live buyer already put a specific number under the ask in writing and offered you the representation — that pair of facts is what moves an institutional seller.

On this board a price question asked and not answered is the strongest form of agreement you get in writing. 🔍 HER WORDS ON THE HOUSE: the buyers “really liked it,” it “showed very well,” and “you can tell they definitely put in the work” — an unprompted compliment to your sellers' prep. ⚠️ THREE CONCERNS, ALL COSMETIC BY HER OWN READ: a crack in the living-room ceiling she thinks is a settled Sheetrock joint; whether crown molding is going back in the living room or being cut in with paint; and a patched ceiling opening in the laundry room she assumes is a deliberate access panel for the bathroom above. 🎯 Two of those are questions only your sellers can answer, and both answers are almost certainly reassuring.
